title: Saturation metrics audit — coverage, label quality, cardinality hotspots (Incident bot + diagnostics)
content:
Context / why this exists
- We’re rolling out saturation collector v1 for the incident bot (ENG-2844) and standardizing saturation dashboards/alerts.
- Before we page harder on saturation, we need confidence in:
  (1) Coverage: metric exists in every region + cluster type
  (2) Label completeness: required dimensions present and consistent
  (3) Cardinality: no accidental explosions that take down the telemetry pipeline
  (4) Semantic correctness: “GPU utilization” vs “queue depth” vs “throttling” aren’t misleading

References
- Saturation signals standard (Confluence): required signals + label guidance
- Dashboards + alert rules: observability-pack/pr_0321
- Cardinality guardrails PR (in flight/landed): redwood/pr_18460

Audit scope (what we checked)
Time window: 2025-01-15 → 2025-02-21 (mix of peak + non-peak)
Regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 (ap-southeast-1 spot-check)
Environments: hosted, dedicated (small sample), private (N/A for centralized metrics; out of scope)
Services: inference-gateway, runtime-scheduler, kv-cache-service, tokenizer-service

Signals in scope (per standard)
1) GPU pressure
- gpu.utilization_pct (device-level)
- gpu.sm_occupancy_pct (preferred for “busy but not blocked”)
- gpu.memory_used_pct
- kv_cache.pressure_pct (runtime-derived)

2) Queueing / throughput
- scheduler.queue_depth (per pool)
- scheduler.queue_wait_ms (p50/p95)
- inference.tokens_per_sec_capacity (estimated)
- inference.tokens_per_sec_actual

3) Throttling / backpressure
- gateway.throttle_429_rate
- scheduler.admission_reject_rate

4) Contention indicators
- scheduler.contention_pct (or contention_seconds)
- runtime.batch_fill_ratio

Required labels (minimum) to make metrics usable in incidents
- region
- env (hosted/dedicated)
- cluster (or pool)
- service
- model_family (NOT full model_id by default)
Optional but frequently requested
- route_group (normalized)
- customer_tier (free/pro/enterprise) (not customer_id)


Summary of findings (high-level)
- Coverage is decent for core GPU/device metrics (util/mem). Weakest is KV cache pressure + scheduler contention (missing or inconsistently emitted in eu-west-1 and in some dedicated pools).
- Label completeness is the #1 issue: region/env/pool are sometimes missing OR use multiple names for the same concept (pool vs cluster vs node_pool).
- Cardinality hotspots were found primarily in:
  - model_id (full) emitted as label in a few metrics
  - route (raw URL path) emitted as label in gateway metrics
  - pod / instance / host labels left unbounded
- Semantics: gpu.utilization_pct is frequently interpreted incorrectly during paging. We should encourage SM occupancy + queueing metrics as the primary “are we saturated?” signal, with utilization as supporting.


Tab: Coverage / quality by metric (notes are intentionally blunt)
Legend
- Coverage: ✅ good / ⚠️ partial / ❌ missing
- Labels: ✅ good / ⚠️ missing/dirty / ❌ unusable
- Cardinality: ✅ safe / ⚠️ watch / ❌ hot

1) gpu.utilization_pct
- Coverage: ✅ (all regions)
- Labels: ⚠️ (env missing in ~12% of series; pool inconsistently named)
- Cardinality: ✅ (device_id present but bounded; acceptable)
- Notes: fine, but noisy for “are we bottlenecked?”

2) gpu.sm_occupancy_pct
- Coverage: ⚠️ (missing in eu-west-1 for some pools; older runtime images)
- Labels: ⚠️ (model_family absent; service sometimes mis-tagged as runtime vs scheduler)
- Cardinality: ✅
- Notes: needs backfill + runtime image upgrade alignment

3) gpu.memory_used_pct
- Coverage: ✅
- Labels: ⚠️ (pool label mismatch)
- Cardinality: ✅

4) kv_cache.pressure_pct
- Coverage: ⚠️ (not emitted for all model architectures; missing entirely for tokenizer-service sidecars)
- Labels: ⚠️ (model_family missing; emitted as model_id in one cluster)
- Cardinality: ❌ (found full model_id label in us-east-1 pool “g6-prod-a”; >800 active series)
- Notes: this is the most likely to blow up dashboards + collector queries

5) scheduler.queue_depth
- Coverage: ✅ (hosted), ⚠️ (dedicated pools emit but with different label set)
- Labels: ⚠️ (pool present, region present, env sometimes absent)
- Cardinality: ✅

6) scheduler.queue_wait_ms (p95)
- Coverage: ⚠️ (not consistently computed in ap-southeast-1)
- Labels: ✅
- Cardinality: ✅

7) inference.tokens_per_sec_capacity
- Coverage: ⚠️ (estimated capacity not emitted in dedicated; some pools emit stale values)
- Labels: ⚠️ (missing model_family; unclear whether per-model or per-pool)
- Cardinality: ✅
- Notes: semantics unclear; needs doc + rename if necessary

8) inference.tokens_per_sec_actual
- Coverage: ✅
- Labels: ⚠️ (route_group missing → teams add raw route label downstream)
- Cardinality: ⚠️ (route label leak in us-west-2 gateway)

9) gateway.throttle_429_rate
- Coverage: ✅
- Labels: ❌ (raw route + customer_id observed in two namespaces)
- Cardinality: ❌ (this is currently a time bomb)
- Notes: must normalize labels before we expand alerting

10) scheduler.contention_pct
- Coverage: ⚠️ (missing in older scheduler builds; not in all regions)
- Labels: ⚠️ (service tag wrong: “scheduler” vs “runtime-scheduler”)
- Cardinality: ✅

11) runtime.batch_fill_ratio
- Coverage: ⚠️ (not available for all runtimes)
- Labels: ✅
- Cardinality: ✅


Cardinality hotspot inventory (what’s exploding and why)
Hotspot A: Raw route labels
- Symptom: label “route” includes full URL path (e.g., /v1/chat/completions, /v1/models/{id}, plus sometimes query params)
- Where: gateway.throttle_429_rate, inference.tokens_per_sec_actual (us-west-2)
- Impact: dashboard queries time out; collector queries expensive; risk of exceeding series limits
- Proposed fix:
  1) replace route with route_group (small allowlist: chat, embeddings, rerank, completions, tokenize, other)
  2) drop query params entirely
  3) enforce label sanitation in telemetry pipeline (Caleb)

Hotspot B: full model_id as label (instead of model_family)
- Symptom: model_id values include version/hash/quantization suffix → series multiplier
- Where: kv_cache.pressure_pct (us-east-1 pool g6-prod-a)
- Proposed fix:
  1) emit model_family only by default
  2) if model_id needed for debugging, emit as EXEMPLAR/log field or behind sampling
  3) add relabel rule: model_id → __dropped__ unless allowlisted

Hotspot C: instance/pod/host leakage
- Symptom: unbounded labels such as pod_name, instance_id, host
- Where: a few GPU metrics in dedicated pools
- Proposed fix:
  - keep device_id if needed; drop pod_name/host; use pool + node_type instead

Hotspot D: customer_id / org_id present
- Symptom: metrics include customer_id label (security + cardinality)
- Where: gateway.throttle_429_rate in two namespaces
- Proposed fix:
  - remove immediately; if we need segmentation use customer_tier only
  - file security note: do not encode customer identifiers into metrics labels


Missing labels / label normalization issues
Observed inconsistencies
- pool label: pool vs node_pool vs cluster
- env label: absent in ~10–15% of series
- region label: present but sometimes “use1/us-east-1/us-east” variants
- service: runtime-scheduler vs scheduler

Proposed normalization contract (for saturation signals)
- region: canonical AWS-style (us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1, ap-southeast-1)
- env: hosted | dedicated
- pool: stable pool identifier (short, no hostnames)
- service: one of inference-gateway | runtime-scheduler | kv-cache-service | tokenizer-service
- model_family: curated list used in Console catalog (e.g., llama3, mistral, qwen2)
- route_group: chat | embeddings | rerank | completions | other

Implementation options
- Best: fix at emission (services) so downstream doesn’t need guesswork
- Also: relabel in telemetry pipeline for guardrails (drop/rename)


Proposed remediation plan (owners + next steps)
P0 — stop the bleeding (1 week)
1) Drop customer_id/org_id labels in gateway metrics
- Owner: Caleb Johnson
- Tracking: ENG-2848 (add subtask)
- Acceptance: confirmed 0 active series with customer_id label in prod metric namespace

2) Route normalization (route → route_group)
- Owner: Caleb Johnson + Chloe Martin (gateway instrumentation)
- Acceptance: for gateway.throttle_429_rate and inference.tokens_per_sec_actual, route_group present; route absent

3) Block model_id label for kv_cache.pressure_pct unless allowlisted
- Owner: Logan Wright (telemetry pipeline) + Jacob Stein (runtime)
- Acceptance: kv_cache.pressure_pct cardinality reduced to <50 series per region per pool (ballpark; depends on pools)

P1 — complete the standard (2–3 weeks)
4) Ensure sm_occupancy emitted in all regions/pools
- Owner: Jacob Stein (runtime) + Devon Price (release coordination)
- Notes: might require runtime image roll forward

5) Fill env/region/service canonical labels
- Owner: Logan Wright
- Acceptance: label completeness dashboard shows >99% series have region+env+pool+service

6) Clarify tokens_per_sec_capacity semantics and rename if needed
- Owner: Allison Grant (spec) + Ravi Menon (architecture review)
- Acceptance: doc update + dashboard label updated; incident responders know what it means

P2 — make it hard to regress (ongoing)
7) Add automated cardinality checks in CI for metric definitions (where possible)
- Owner: Logan Wright
- Acceptance: PR checklist + automated “top N series contributors” report for saturation namespace

8) Add “label allowlist” gate for saturation namespace
- Owner: Logan Wright
- Acceptance: new labels cannot land without explicit approval (lightweight review)


Collector implications (Incident bot saturation collector v1)
- Collector queries must be resilient + low-cardinality.
- Proposed query inputs (safe-by-default): region, env, pool, service, route_group, model_family.
- Collector must not query by model_id or raw route.
- If metrics are delayed/missing: fail open with an explicit “data delayed / not emitted in this region yet” section.

Open questions
- Do we need per-model saturation breakdowns in incident threads, or is per-pool sufficient for first 2–5 minutes?
  - SRE preference (Rafael): per-pool first; per-model only on-demand via command.
- Dedicated env: should we unify label set with hosted even if internals differ?
  - Likely yes; otherwise responders will distrust dashboards.
- KV cache pressure: how do we define it across model architectures consistently?
  - Might need “kv_cache.hit_rate” vs “pressure” split; revisit after P1.


Appendix: quick checks / how we measured
- Used ad-hoc queries in the metrics explorer to list label keys and top cardinality contributors.
- Sample approach:
  - For each metric: count distinct(label) over 1h window; compare across regions.
  - List top label values by series count for suspected offenders (model_id, route, pod).
- Saved screenshots live in Slack thread (eng-sre/1707520099_331221) (not attached here).

Change log
- 2025-01-29: created doc (Allison)
- 2025-02-06: added hotspot sections + P0 plan after seeing customer_id label leak (Caleb)
- 2025-02-18: updated findings after eu-west-1 spot-check; noted sm_occupancy gaps (Jacob)
- 2025-02-24: tightened acceptance criteria + linked to guardrails PR (Logan)
